prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract with You” (policy measures only)

Core pledges
- Freeze most immigration; stop small-boat crossings via detention, deportation, and returns to France.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; lift higher-rate threshold to £70,000.
- Cut energy levies and end Net Zero policies; expand UK oil and gas.
- Fund changes via waste cuts and regulatory reform.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential immigration; create a Department of Immigration.
- Leave ECHR; bar asylum from safe countries; offshore rapid processing; no legal aid for non-citizens.
- Deport foreign offenders after sentences; remove citizenship for serious crimes.
- Restrict student dependants; close abuse of routes; 5-year residency and work test for benefits.
- Employer Immigration Tax: NI at 20% for foreign workers (exempt essential health/care and very small firms).
- Claimed impact: £5–10bn savings pa; £4bn revenue pa.

Government waste and regulation
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to commercial banks (£35bn pa).
- 5% efficiency saving across departments and quangos (£50bn pa).
- Halve foreign aid (£6bn pa); accelerate removal of retained EU law; improve HMRC tax collection.
- Total potential savings claimed: £91bn pa (within this section).

Economy – personal and business
- Personal: lift tax thresholds; cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy; remove green levies; cut/rescale Stamp Duty; restore VAT-free tourist shopping; raise IHT threshold to £2m and cut rate above to 20%. Cost: £70bn pa.
- Business: raise CT threshold to £100k profit; cut main CT to 20% then 15%; abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high-street SMEs with a 4% online delivery tax; planning and deregulatory reforms. Cost: £18bn pa.

NHS
- Zero basic-rate income tax for frontline NHS and social care staff for 3 years; expand training; student fee write-offs tied to service.
- Use independent capacity (UK/overseas); 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Voucher if waits exceed 3 days (GP), 3 weeks (consultant), 9 weeks (operation); efficiency and procurement reforms; “Pharmacy First.” Cost: £17bn pa.

Energy/Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero targets and related subsidies; tax renewables equivalently.
- Fast-track North Sea oil/gas; pilot shale; accelerate SMRs and other generation. Claimed savings: £30bn pa.

Policing and justice
- 40,000 extra officers over 5 years; “zero-tolerance” emphasis; expand stop and search; mandatory life for drug dealing/trafficking; new “substantial possession” offence with heavy fines; reduce DEI roles; standards and training reforms. Cost: £3bn pa.
- Justice: tougher sentencing for violent repeat offenders; increase budget to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; build 10,000 detention places; family court and grooming-gang reforms. Cost: £2bn pa.

Education
- Curriculum review; rules on gender questioning and single-sex facilities; parental notification under 16.
- 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap student loan interest; longer repayment; minimum entry standards; stronger free-speech enforcement; more PRUs; optional 2-year degrees. Cost: £5bn pa.

Welfare
- Stronger work incentives and compliance (two-offer rule; face-to-face assessments). Claimed savings: £15bn pa.

Brexit and constitutional
- Scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate TCA; distance from EU defence structures.
- Leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act; reform House of Lords and Civil Service leadership; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights. Cost: neutral.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay uplift; Armed Forces Justice Bill; dedicated Veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform; skills/education. Cost: £14bn pa.

Housing
- Fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals for social housing; restore landlords’ mortgage interest relief; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold protections. Cost: neutral.

Families
- Transferable marriage allowance (25%) when affordable; front-load Child Benefit (ages 1–4); single-sex spaces; measures on child online harms. Cost: £8bn pa.

Transport and utilities
- Scrap remaining HS2 (£25bn one-off saving); limit ULEZ/LTNs; no new ICE bans; regional infrastructure focus; new 50/50 public–pension fund ownership model for utilities; cap standing charges. Savings: £25bn one-off, £5bn pa.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farming budget to £3bn; shift subsidies; cut red tape; domestic sourcing targets; CMA powers on pricing. Cost: £2bn pa.
- End automatic foreign access to UK waters; licence/fees; enforcement; ban supertrawlers and pulse fishing; rebuild processing/fleet. Cost: £2bn pa.

Pensions and social care
- Royal Commission; tackle offshore tax practices in care; pension system review; implement 2021 Mineworkers’ recommendations.

Reclaiming Britain
- Oppose WHO treaty and CBDC; replace Equalities Act/DEI rules; free speech bill; reform BBC incl. ending licence fee; new anti-corruption unit; St George’s and St David’s Day holidays.

Funding summary (party’s figures)
- Claimed savings: £150bn pa + £10bn pa from extra growth = £160bn pa.
- Claimed costs: £141bn pa.
